messages:
alejandra (Identity): FYI customer started seeing 403s after IdP cert rotation. Our auth logs show a "Recipient mismatch" error. They rotated yesterday and failures began ~09:12 UTC.
maria (Support): Can you paste the raw auth log line? Need to know if it failed on signature or recipient check.
alejandra (Identity): Log: ```SAMLResponse validation failed: AssertionRecipientMismatch: expected 'https://app.redwood.example/sso/acs' got 'https://app.redwood.example/sso/acs?sid=abc123'```

jason (SRE): Looks like their IdP started appending a session id to the ACS URL. We usually normalize, but our recipient check is strict. Any chance they changed ACS behavior during rotation?
maria (Support): Customer confirms they republished metadata and enabled a session-index param at the same time they rotated keys.

tony (Eng): @jason what's the risk of loosening recipient equality? Stripping querystrings could mask redirect attacks.
jason (SRE): Short term we can implement a safe normalization: if host+path match a registered ACS, accept querystring differences for that customer only. Long term we should tighten allowed patterns in the console.
alejandra (Identity): Also spotted metadata author uploaded both old and new signing keys, but left the old key first. Our verifier tries the first key and gave up; some responses were signed by the new key so it failed inconsistently.
maria (Support): Stack trace: ```Signature validation: tried cert thumbprint AB:CD:... -> no match; tried next cert -> matched -> but we returned recipient mismatch earlier``` — both signature ordering and recipient strictness combined to block traffic.

alejandra (Identity): Repro steps I ran:
1) curl metadata from https://idp.customer.example/metadata.xml
2) Observe <KeyDescriptor use="signing"> old-key then new-key
3) Craft SAMLResponse signed with new key and ACS with ?sid param
4) POST to /sso/acs -> AssertionRecipientMismatch then signature fallback

jason (SRE): Deployed a canary mitigation in us-west:
- Allow recipient match ignoring querystring for known registrants
- Attempt signature verification against all signing KeyDescriptor entries

deploy-bot: canary deploy identity-tolerant-recipient v2026.3 started -> instances i-0a123,i-0b456

maria (Support): Customer reports failures drop from ~120/min to ~3/min after canary. They still see occasional 403 when responses are signed with the old cert id but reference a different KeyInfo id.

alejandra (Identity): Root cause summary: three simultaneous changes from IdP rotation: (1) appended session query param on ACS posts, (2) new signing key added but old key left first in metadata, (3) a gradual mix of signing certs during rollout. Our pipeline assumed single key ordering + strict recipient equality so failures were common.

tony (Eng): Action items:
- Short: keep canary 24h then expand if stable (jason)
- Short: metadata verifier should try all signing keys (alejandra)
- Short: add allowlist normalization that strips querystrings only when host+path matches registered ACS (security review) (tony)
- Long: telemetry to detect mixed-key signing during rotations (maria)

jason (SRE): INFRA-3921 opened. Rolling canary to 50% now.
maria (Support): Sent guidance to customer: either publish new key first in metadata, avoid appending session params to ACS, or ask us to add exact ACS pattern to allowlist.

alejandra (Identity): Enabled feature-flag to try-all-keys for this tenant. PR: https://git.redwood/infr/identity/merge/498

tony (Eng): Security note: normalization must not drop path differences; only strip query and fragment. Will draft a short RFC for review.

maria (Support): Customer disabled the session param append and republished metadata with new key first. Confirmed full recovery. Marking support ticket resolved.

sre-oncall (bot): Incident closed. Duration ~3h 32m. (reaction :hourglass_flowing_sand:)
